description: User Language programs shipped with EAGLE 9.6.0 in <EAGLE>\examples\ulps\examples, part B: board and schematic editing helpers (teardrops, renumbering, find, width/class/layer changes, silkscreen and mask generation, snapping, panelizing, coils and RF stubs), schematic/board consistency tools, library building and maintenance programs, German electrical-drawing tools and the User Language programming examples. Run them with RUN <file>.ulp [args] in the matching editor; most generate editor commands and hand them back with exit().

tools.name: teardrops.ulp
tools.description: Adds teardrop-shaped connections between vias/pads and their attached wire segments, which improves manufacturability when a drill is slightly off-centre. The dialog selects vias and/or pads and the layers to process and generates a script that draws the teardrops.
tools.usage: RUN teardrops.ulp   (Board Editor; dialog: Teardrop Vias, Teardrop Pads, layers)
tools.example: RUN teardrops.ulp
tools.notes: Run DRC afterwards; teardrops are ordinary wires of the signal. Version 1.05 by Tad Artis with later modifications.

tools.name: cmd-renumber.ulp
tools.description: Renumbers the components of a board by position, starting from any corner (top/bottom, left/right), scanning horizontally or vertically within a scan window, so that reference designators follow the physical layout. Use it after placement so that designators are easy to find on the assembled board.
tools.usage: RUN cmd-renumber.ulp   (Board Editor; dialog: units, direction, start corner, scan window)
tools.example: RUN cmd-renumber.ulp
tools.notes: Generates NAME commands (via temporary $$ names), so with forward/back annotation the schematic follows. See the ULP's built-in help for the scan-window options.

tools.name: renumber-sheet.ulp
tools.description: Renumbers schematic parts sheet by sheet using each device set's prefix, sorted by coordinates; it first checks for empty or inconsistent prefixes, can open the device in the library to fix the prefix and update the library. An optional start offset gives per-sheet ranges such as R101..R199 on sheet 1 and R201..R299 on sheet 2.
tools.usage: RUN renumber-sheet.ulp   (Schematic Editor; follow the dialog steps)
tools.example: RUN renumber-sheet.ulp   # offset 100 -> sheet 1: R101.., sheet 2: R201..
tools.notes: Parts with and without packages are renumbered; supply symbols are not.

tools.name: find.ulp
tools.description: Finds devices, parts, nets, buses, pins, pads, signals or values in a schematic, board or library object, centres and zooms to the hit, and can step through several hits. It can also search drills, via stacks and polygon widths, list or place unused gates, and replace values (VALUE old CH new). cmd-showzoom.ulp is a simpler board-only 'show and zoom' variant.
tools.usage: RUN find [ name [ pin | pad | [value [current_value [CH new_value]] [ count | * ]] | RUN find [DEV|GATE|PIN|PAD|POLYGON width|DRILL diameter|VIA stack|value [-S|+|-] [counter|*]]
tools.example:
RUN find R12
RUN find DRILL 0.8 *
RUN find VALUE 10k CH 12k
tools.notes: default-assign.scr binds it to Ctrl+F (ASSIGN C+F 'RUN find.ulp'). CH is case-sensitive.

tools.name: find-single-ended-wire.ulp
tools.description: Finds wire stubs, i.e. wires that do not start or end at another wire, via or pad. Without parameters it builds a list; + and - step through it showing only the relevant layer, M groups the stub and activates MOVE so it can be selected easily and removed with RIPUP.
tools.example:
RATSNEST
RUN find-single-ended-wire
RUN find-single-ended-wire +
tools.notes: Wires or vias ending inside a polygon count as single-ended: run RATSNEST first. Set the layer fill to hatched/dotted to see stubs. Since 9.1 the DRC also warns about wire stubs.

tools.name: cmd-change-brd-width.ulp
tools.description: Changes the width of routed wires of selected signals whose current width lies between a minimum and a maximum value, for example to widen all power traces in one step. Net-name checking can be switched off (NameOff = 1) to process all signals.
tools.example: RUN cmd-change-brd-width.ulp   # signals GND, VCC: 0.2-0.3 mm -> 0.6 mm
tools.notes: Run DRC afterwards for clearance violations.

tools.name: cmd-change-class.ulp
tools.description: Changes the net classes of signals in a board through a dialog, with units selectable as MIC, MM, MIL or INCH. Use it to reassign many signals at once instead of one by one.
tools.example: RUN cmd-change-class.ulp
tools.notes: export-class.ulp saves classes as a script for reuse.

tools.name: cmd-change-swap-layer.ulp
tools.description: Moves all objects from one layer to another: copper objects only to other copper layers and non-copper objects only to non-copper layers. Use it, for example, to move a drawing to another documentation layer or to swap the contents of two inner copper layers.
tools.example: RUN cmd-change-swap-layer.ulp   # move everything from layer 2 to layer 15
tools.notes: Check the result with DRC, especially for vias and polygons.

tools.name: change-via-by-stack.ulp
tools.description: Changes drill, diameter and shape, or the layer span (stack), of all vias that have a given start and end layer, which is handy for blind and buried vias. Omitted drill/diameter values take the current CHANGE defaults; NO keeps them and only changes the shape.
tools.usage: RUN change-via-by-stack Start-Layer End-Layer [[Drill [Diameter [NO] [Shape]]]] | RUN change-via-by-stack Start End Newstart-Newend STACK
tools.example:
RUN change-via-by-stack 1 2 0.1 0.15 SQUARE
RUN change-via-by-stack 1 2 1-16 STACK
tools.notes: The #usage text is mostly German; options are case-insensitive.

tools.name: cmd-change-value-group.ulp
tools.description: Sets the value of all elements in the current GROUP, optionally only those whose name starts with a given prefix. It works in the board and in the schematic.
tools.example:
GROUP (draw around the resistors)
RUN cmd-change-value-group 4k7 R
tools.notes: Works in board and schematic sheet contexts.

tools.name: change-prefix-sch.ulp
tools.description: Changes the name prefix of parts in a schematic, e.g. renaming all IC parts to U, by generating the NAME commands. Run it in the Schematic Editor; with forward/back annotation the board elements are renamed as well.
tools.example: RUN change-prefix-sch IC U
tools.notes: Change the device set PREFIX in the library as well if new parts should follow the new convention.

tools.name: copy-wire-to-any-layer.ulp and copy-wire-to-solder-mask.ulp
tools.description: Copy the copper wires and/or polygons of selected signals from layer 1 or 16 into another layer: copy-wire-to-any-layer.ulp to any layer (also copying rectangles, circles and texts when the target is not copper), copy-wire-to-solder-mask.ulp into the stop-mask layers to keep those traces free of solder resist (e.g. for extra tin). Both run in the Board Editor.

parameters.name: -p / +p
parameters.description: Also copy polygons / copy only polygons.

parameters.name: -f / +f
parameters.description: Polygon contour only as polygon / contour and filling as wires.

tools.example: run copy-wire-to-solder-mask.ulp -p GND VBUS
tools.notes: Options are case-sensitive.

tools.name: panelize.ulp and copy-silk-screen.ulp
tools.description: Preparation for panelizing a board with GROUP/CUT/PASTE: panelize.ulp copies the name texts of all elements into new layers 125 and 126, copy-silk-screen.ulp copies names, values, place and docu graphics into new layers (+100). The copies keep the original names when the board is pasted several times, so every copy in the panel shows identical silkscreen.
tools.usage: RUN panelize.ulp | RUN copy-silk-screen.ulp   (Board Editor; display all layers first)
tools.example:
RUN panelize.ulp
# then GROUP, CUT and PASTE the layout into an array
# CAM: use layers 125/126 instead of 25/26
tools.notes: Texts must be smashed (automatic since 9.2). Deactivate the original layers (25/26, or 21-28 and 51-52) and activate the new ones in the CAM job.

tools.name: silk.ulp
tools.description: Creates a wider silkscreen for manufacturers that need at least 8 mil lines: all objects of tPlace/bPlace are copied into new layers 121 (_tplace) and 122 (_bplace) with a minimum width of 8 mil, and texts get ratio 16%. Use it when a manufacturer rejects thin silkscreen lines.
tools.example:
RUN silk.ulp
# CAM: output layers 121/122 instead of 21/22
tools.notes: EAGLE libraries use 5 mil silkscreen lines by default.

tools.name: normalize-text.ulp
tools.description: Normalizes silkscreen texts: all texts on the silkscreen layers are set to the same size and stroke thickness, with the ratio calculated from the desired thickness. It smashes the texts first so that each can be changed individually.
tools.example: RUN normalize-text.ulp   # 1.0 mm size, 0.15 mm stroke
tools.notes: By Tennessee Carmel-Veilleux.

tools.name: spin-all.ulp
tools.description: Sets or clears the spin flag on all (smashed) texts of the board by generating a command sequence (layer by layer, ROTATE SR0 on each text whose flag must toggle). A text with the spin flag may be shown upside down instead of being turned automatically to stay readable.
tools.example: RUN spin-all OFF
tools.notes: ON/OFF are not case-sensitive.

tools.name: copy-text-as-wire.ulp and cmd-place-restrict-name-value.ulp
tools.description: Convert texts into wire geometry in other layers: copy-text-as-wire.ulp copies the vector strokes of layout texts into user layers, and cmd-place-restrict-name-value.ulp copies the name and value texts of all elements into the restrict layers 41 and 42 so the autorouter keeps the text areas free. Both generate command sequences that are executed when the ULP ends.
tools.example:
RUN cmd-place-restrict-name-value.ulp
AUTO;
tools.notes: Generated wires are ordinary objects; remove them with DISPLAY <layer> only, GROUP, DELETE.

tools.name: cmd-draw-polygon-contours-as-wire.ulp
tools.description: Draws the calculated contours of a signal's polygon as wires, optionally including the filling, into the same or another layer, for example for milling or documentation. Run it in the Board Editor with the signal name as argument.
tools.example:
RATSNEST
RUN cmd-draw-polygon-contours-as-wire GND FILLING 150
tools.notes: Calculate polygons with RATSNEST first.

tools.name: maskdata.ulp, via-mask-one-layer.ulp and fill-via4vacuum.ulp
tools.description: Mask-related generators: maskdata.ulp writes maskdata.scr, which creates new layers with individual solder-stop and cream symbols that can be edited one by one; via-mask-one-layer.ulp draws a one-sided stop-mask opening in tStop or bStop with a given width from the drill edge; fill-via4vacuum.ulp builds a mask in a user layer to fill vias for a vacuum adapter. All three work in the Board Editor.
tools.usage: RUN maskdata.ulp | RUN via-mask-one-layer.ulp (it saves the design rules with DRC SAVE and restarts itself) | RUN fill-via4vacuum.ulp [userlayer]
tools.example:
RUN maskdata.ulp
SCRIPT maskdata.scr
tools.notes: Octagon pads get a round stop symbol in maskdata. Remove generated objects with DISPLAY <layer> only, GROUP, DELETE, then LAYER -<number>.

tools.name: make-long-pad-inner-layer.ulp
tools.description: Gives LONG and OFFSET pads in inner layers the same shape as on the outer layers by adding wire segments (EAGLE otherwise uses round pads in inner layers), so the DRC and polygon calculation respect slotted holes drawn in layer 46 Milling. Give element names to limit it to those parts, or none to process all elements with long pads.
tools.example: RUN make-long-pad-inner-layer X1 X2
tools.notes: Inner layers must be in use with at least one wire or polygon. The extension can connect fully to a plane where thermals were expected; check with DRC.

tools.name: component-array.ulp
tools.description: Arranges components that are already placed on the board into circular or rectangular arrays, for example LED rings or connector rows. It works in the Board Editor through a dialog.
tools.example: RUN component-array.ulp   # LED1..LED12 on a circle of radius 20 mm
tools.notes: Since 9.2 the PATTERN command offers linear and circular copies of objects.

tools.name: cmd-draw.ulp
tools.description: Drawing helper for boards, schematics and packages: draws or places wires, polygons, circles, ellipses and quarter ellipses, pads, SMDs or vias at a distance/radius with start, step and end angles, rotates and pastes groups, or moves elements into place by order. Coordinates are relative when a MARK is set.
tools.usage: RUN cmd-draw.ulp   (dialog; options in any order, not case-sensitive)
tools.example:
MARK (0 0)
RUN cmd-draw.ulp   # 12 pads on radius 10 mm, 30 degree step
tools.notes: The many cmd-draw-*.bmp files next to the ULP illustrate the options.

tools.name: spiral-coil.ulp, print-inductor.ulp and microstrip-radial-stub.ulp
tools.description: Copper geometry generators: spiral-coil.ulp and print-inductor.ulp calculate and draw printed coils (print-inductor with or without a ferrite core), placing pads when started in the library or vias when started in a board; microstrip-radial-stub.ulp draws a microstrip radial stub. They produce geometry only; confirm the electrical values by measurement.
tools.usage: RUN spiral-coil.ulp | RUN print-inductor.ulp | RUN microstrip-radial-stub   (board or package editor; dialog)
tools.example: RUN spiral-coil.ulp   # 10 turns, 0.3 mm track, 0.3 mm gap
tools.notes: The inductance formula is an approximation; material, layer thickness, copper areas and frequency matter, so verify by measurement. Printed coils are mainly useful in the MHz range.

tools.name: cmd-snap-board.ulp, snap-on-grid-sch.ulp, cmd-snappads.ulp and snap-pin-in-symbol.ulp
tools.description: Grid-snapping helpers: cmd-snap-board.ulp snaps components, wires and vias of a board to a grid (the MOVE commands can be edited before running), snap-on-grid-sch.ulp snaps symbols, junctions, nets and buses of a schematic to a grid (default 0.1 inch), cmd-snappads.ulp snaps pads and SMDs in the package editor (separate x and y grids) and snap-pin-in-symbol.ulp snaps symbol pins. Start each one in the matching editor.
tools.usage: RUN cmd-snap-board.ulp | RUN snap-on-grid-sch.ulp | RUN cmd-snappads.ulp | run snap-pin-in-symbol [100]
tools.example:
EDIT OPAMP.sym
run snap-pin-in-symbol 100
tools.notes: Off-grid pins are a common cause of unconnected nets; fix them in the library.

tools.name: make-group2pac.ulp
tools.description: Generates a package (footprint) from the pads of a GROUP of elements selected in the layout; layer 20 Dimension is always included and holes and texts can be grouped too. Useful to turn a hand-drawn arrangement into a library footprint.
tools.example:
GROUP (around the connector pads)
RUN make-group2pac.ulp
tools.notes: The #usage text is English and German.

tools.name: make-value-consistent.ulp and make-package-consistent-brd-sch.ulp
tools.description: Repair tools for inconsistent schematic/board pairs: make-value-consistent.ulp copies values from the editor it is started in to the other, and make-package-consistent-brd-sch.ulp makes the schematic use the packages found in the board. Use them when schematic and board disagree about values or packages.
tools.usage: RUN make-value-consistent.ulp (in the editor with the correct values) | RUN make-package-consistent-brd-sch.ulp
tools.example: RUN make-value-consistent.ulp
tools.notes: Back up both files first and run ERC afterwards.

tools.name: copy-attrib-sch-to-brd.ulp
tools.description: Copies all part attributes from the schematic to the corresponding board elements, a simple fix for attribute inconsistencies; it does not check what already exists on the board. Start it from the schematic with the board loaded as well.
tools.example: RUN copy-attrib-sch-to-brd.ulp
tools.notes: By Jorge Garcia (2016).

tools.name: show-group.ulp and select-sch-group-to-brd-group.ulp
tools.description: Cross-probing between editors: show-group.ulp highlights in the board the objects of a group selected in the schematic (or the reverse), and select-sch-group-to-brd-group.ulp defines a GROUP in the layout containing the elements grouped in the schematic and activates MOVE so they can be moved together (Ctrl+right-click). Use them to find the board counterparts of a schematic block.
tools.usage: GROUP in one editor; RUN show-group.ulp or RUN select-sch-group-to-brd-group in the other
tools.example:
# schematic: GROUP the power-supply parts
# board:
RUN select-sch-group-to-brd-group
tools.notes: Needs a consistent schematic/board pair.

tools.name: showclass.ulp
tools.description: Highlights all nets or signals that belong to a given net class, in a schematic or a board. It helps to review which nets belong to power or other special classes.
tools.example: RUN showclass 1
tools.notes: Without an argument a dialog asks for the class.

tools.name: trace-layer.ulp
tools.description: Steps through the board layers one at a time to inspect them; layers 17 Pads, 18 Vias, 19 Unrouted, 23 tOrigins and 24 bOrigins are not shown separately. Use it to review the layers of a board in turn.
tools.example:
ASSIGN F9 'RUN trace-layer +;'
ASSIGN F10 'RUN trace-layer -;'
tools.notes: Handy with ASSIGNed keys.

tools.name: layer-sequence.ulp and print-transparent-brd.ulp
tools.description: Printing helpers: layer-sequence.ulp edits Option.LayerSequence in eaglerc.usr, which defines the order in which layers are rendered on printers, PDF and PostScript (e.g. '123b * 123t' renders layer 123 first); print-transparent-brd.ulp prints a board 'transparently' with weakened copper colours under a black assembly print, or with IMAGE writes a PNG at a chosen resolution. Both affect printed or exported output only, not the design data.
tools.usage: RUN layer-sequence.ulp | RUN print-transparent-brd [Options] | RUN print-transparent-brd IMAGE @ DPI [Options]
tools.example: RUN print-transparent-brd IMAGE @ 360
tools.notes: print-transparent-brd's help is German; its other options are passed to PRINT (see HELP PRINT). Only the IMAGE option is truly transparent.

tools.name: exp-palette.ulp
tools.description: Exports the current colour palette, or all palettes, as an EAGLE script file that can be run with SCRIPT on another installation. Use it to back up colours or carry them to another installation.
tools.example:
RUN exp-palette.ulp
# elsewhere: SCRIPT mypalette.scr
tools.notes: defaultcolors.scr and legacycolors.scr are shipped palette scripts of the same kind.

tools.name: mirror-board-remirror-element-swap-layer.ulp
tools.description: Creates a mirror-image layout, e.g. the right-hand version of a left-hand headlight board: it mirrors the whole board, mirrors the components back at their origins and redraws the traces mirrored without swapping top and bottom. It then runs DRC so that overlaps show where traces no longer meet the pads.
tools.example:
RUN mirror-board-remirror-element-swap-layer.ulp
ERRORS
tools.notes: Help text is German. Symmetric two-pin parts work directly (horizontal ones need a 180 degree rotation); asymmetric or multi-row parts such as SOT23 or SO14 need rerouting.

tools.name: rename-signal.ulp and renamnet-suffix.ulp
tools.description: Append a suffix to names: rename-signal.ulp renames all signals of a board with a suffix (close the schematic first), renamnet-suffix.ulp renames nets of a schematic with a suffix, handling nets spread over several segments or sheets. Both generate the rename commands automatically.
tools.usage: RUN rename-signal.ulp [suffix] (the #usage calls it rename-signals) | RUN renamnet-suffix.ulp
tools.example: RUN rename-signal.ulp _B
tools.notes: Useful before merging two boards or schematics that use the same net names.

tools.name: net-bus-labeling.ulp
tools.description: Places LABELs automatically at the grouped ends of net and bus wires: define a GROUP that includes only one end of each wire, and a label is placed there with an offset (10 mil for nets, 20 mil for buses), rotated with the wire, text size 70 mil. It saves placing many labels by hand after drawing a bus breakout.
tools.usage: GROUP (around the wire ends); RUN net-bus-labeling.ulp   (Schematic Editor)
tools.example:
GROUP (box around the bus entry ends)
RUN net-bus-labeling.ulp
tools.notes: Help text is German. Since 8.7 NAME on nets and buses can also place labels automatically.

tools.name: make-symbol-device-package-bsdl.ulp
tools.description: Builds a symbol and device from a text file listing pin names (e.g. copied from a data sheet or spreadsheet), and can create the package too: a BGA from a BSDL (Boundary Scan Description Language) file, or dual/quad packages from parameters; alternatively it uses an existing package in the library. It is the quickest way to create parts with very many pins, such as FPGAs.
tools.example:
OPEN myfpga.lbr
RUN make-symbol-device-package-bsdl.ulp   # load myfpga.bsd, generate BGA package + device
tools.notes: Split an oversized symbol afterwards with split-device-symbol.ulp.

tools.name: split-device-symbol.ulp and connect-device-split-symbol.ulp
tools.description: After a large symbol has been divided into several smaller symbols with GROUP, CUT, EDIT xx.sym and PASTE, these ULPs generate the CONNECT list for a new multi-gate device by adopting the connects of the original device. The two files are near-identical variants.
tools.usage: RUN split-device-symbol.ulp | RUN connect-device-split-symbol.ulp   (Library Editor, new device)
tools.example:
EDIT BIGCHIP-SPLIT.dev
RUN split-device-symbol.ulp
tools.notes: Pin names must be unique, so devices with identical gates (NAND, op-amps) are not supported; existing connects of the target variant cause an error.

tools.name: exp-lbrs.ulp
tools.description: Exports the libraries used in a schematic and/or board into one or several .lbr files so components can be changed individually, then brought back with UPDATE. When exporting into several libraries it also writes a replace script (<schematic>_ReplaceLibParts.scr), which helps converting older projects to libraries with 3D packages.
tools.usage: RUN exp-lbrs.ulp   (Schematic or Board Editor; also File > Export > Libraries)
tools.notes: Improved in 8.5/8.6 for managed libraries.

tools.name: check-used-lbrs.ulp
tools.description: Lists the components of the current schematic or board whose library component can no longer be found in the available libraries, for example after libraries were renamed or reorganized. Use it before running UPDATE to find parts that would not be updated.
tools.example: RUN check-used-lbrs.ulp
tools.notes: The comparison is case-sensitive.

tools.name: remove-unused-packages.ulp and update-packages.ulp
tools.description: Package maintenance: remove-unused-packages.ulp deletes the package variants of a placed device's library that the design does not use and then runs UPDATE; update-packages.ulp updates the footprints of the current library from a reference package library with UPDATE and WRITE. Both change library files, so work on copies.
tools.usage: RUN remove-unused-packages [Prefix | Partname] | RUN update-packages.ulp (Library Editor)
tools.example: RUN remove-unused-packages R
tools.notes: remove-unused-packages modifies the library: copy it to a separate folder and point Options > Directories there first. update-packages uses the reference library named in its source (plcc-socket.lbr, which is not shipped), so edit that name before use.

tools.name: change-pad-in-lbr.ulp and clear-layer-in-lbr.ulp
tools.description: Bulk library edits: change-pad-in-lbr.ulp changes shape, diameter, flags and drill of all pads in a library (drills within given tolerances, rounded to 0.1 mm, annular rings within a range); clear-layer-in-lbr.ulp generates a script that deletes everything on the given layers in all packages. Both run in the Library Editor.
tools.example:
OPEN mylib.lbr
run clear-layer-in-lbr.ulp 51 52
tools.notes: YES clears without confirmation. Work on a copy of the library.

tools.name: del-devices.ulp, del-empty-devices.ulp and del-pack-sym.ulp
tools.description: Library clean-up: del-devices.ulp deletes chosen devices, del-empty-devices.ulp deletes devices without a symbol, and del-pack-sym.ulp deletes unused packages and symbols. Each shows the generated DELETE commands in an editor window for review and runs them on EXECUTE.
tools.usage: RUN del-devices.ulp | RUN del-empty-devices.ulp | RUN del-pack-sym.ulp   (Library Editor)
tools.example:
OPEN mylib.lbr
RUN del-pack-sym.ulp   # review list, EXECUTE
tools.notes: Objects in use cannot be deleted; keep Enter pressed to acknowledge those messages.

tools.name: set-all-devices-attribute.ulp
tools.description: Runs a script through all device sets and technologies of a library to define attributes. The script contains lines ATTRIBUTE name 'value' or ATTRIBUTE name DELETE; existing attributes and lines without a value are left unchanged.
tools.example:
# attr.scr: ATTRIBUTE MANUFACTURER 'ACME'
RUN set-all-devices-attribute attr.scr
tools.notes: Separate words by exactly one space and always quote the value.

tools.name: run-loop-all-*.ulp (script and ULP loops)
tools.description: Batch runners: run-loop-all-devicesets-script, run-loop-all-packages-script and run-loop-all-symbols-script run a script on every device set, package or symbol of the open library; run-loop-all-lbr-script and run-loop-all-lbr-ulp run a script or ULP on every library in a directory; run-loop-all-schematic-script runs a script on every schematic in the project directory. They let one script or ULP change a whole library or a folder of files in a single run.
tools.usage: RUN run-loop-all-devicesets-script [SCRIPT] | RUN run-loop-all-packages-script [SCRIPT] | RUN run-loop-all-symbols-script [SCRIPT] | RUN run-loop-all-lbr-script | RUN run-loop-all-lbr-ulp | RUN run-loop-all-schematic-script
tools.example:
OPEN mylib.lbr
RUN run-loop-all-packages-script fix-silk.scr
tools.notes: Start the directory loops from any library/schematic in that directory. The #usage of run-loop-all-packages-script says 'symbols' by mistake.

tools.name: exp-descr-html.ulp and exp-descr-script.ulp
tools.description: Export device and package descriptions of a library: exp-descr-html.ulp as HTML, exp-descr-script.ulp as a script that can be edited in a text editor and read back with SCRIPT to update the descriptions. Both run in the Library Editor.
tools.example:
OPEN mylib.lbr
RUN exp-descr-script.ulp
# edit the exported script in a text editor, then read it back with SCRIPT <file>.scr
tools.notes: Descriptions are searched by the ADD dialog, so good descriptions pay off.

tools.name: generate-dummy-package-and-connect.ulp
tools.description: For electrical-drawing devices: creates a dummy package for the current device whose pad names equal the symbol pin names, named after the device, and connects pins to pads. Start it after creating the device and adding the symbols. e-packages-aus-devices-pin-ist-padname.ulp is the German twin.
tools.example:
EDIT RELAY-K1.dev
ADD COIL K 0 NEXT (0 0)
RUN generate-dummy-package-and-connect.ulp
tools.notes: Pin names must be unique.

tools.name: set_name_value.ulp
tools.description: Places the >NAME and >VALUE placeholder texts in the current package or symbol if they are missing: in a symbol on layers 95 Names and 96 Values with 70 mil text, in a package on layers 25 tNames and 27 tValues with 50 mil text. Run it in the Package or Symbol Editor when those texts are missing.
tools.example:
EDIT SO08.fpt
RUN set_name_value.ulp
tools.notes: Combine with run-loop-all-packages-script or run-loop-all-symbols-script for a whole library.

tools.name: Library navigation ULPs (editnext/editprev, next/prev descript, edit-used-dev-pac-sym)
tools.description: Small navigation helpers mostly bound to keys by lbr-assign.scr: editnext-/editprev-dev-sym-pac.ulp open the next/previous device, symbol or package, editnext-/editprev-lbr.ulp the next/previous library in the directory, editnext-/editprev-sheet.ulp the next/previous schematic sheet, next/prevdevdescript.ulp and next/prevpacdescript.ulp edit the next/previous description, cmd-rename-in-lbr.ulp renames and remove-dev-sym-pac.ulp removes the current object, and edit-used-dev-pac-sym.ulp opens the library object used by a part. Load lbr-assign.scr to have them one keystroke away.
tools.example:
SCRIPT lbr-assign.scr   # Ctrl+N / Ctrl+P = next / previous object
RUN edit-used-dev-pac-sym U1 @
tools.notes: edit-used-dev-pac-sym opens a new drawing with the object name if the library is not found in the library path.

tools.name: e-*.ulp (German electrical-drawing tools)
tools.description: Programs for electrical schematics made with the elektro libraries (German help): e-attributverwaltung manages local and global attributes such as frame data, e-brueckenverwaltung defines jumper bridges in terminal blocks (<schematic>.brk), e-klemmenplan creates a terminal plan of all point-to-point connections, e-makelist puts those lists onto schematic sheets, and e-bauteil-erstellen builds devices (e.g. contactors) with dummy packages from existing symbols. They run in the Schematic or Library Editor and are documented only in German.
tools.usage: RUN e-attributverwaltung.ulp | RUN e-brueckenverwaltung.ulp | RUN e-klemmenplan.ulp | RUN e-makelist.ulp | RUN e-bauteil-erstellen.ulp
tools.example:
SCRIPT elektro-init.scr   # adds a Tools menu for e-attributverwaltung, e-brueckenverwaltung and e-klemmenplan
RUN e-klemmenplan.ulp
tools.notes: See projects\examples\elektro\stern-dreieck-anlauf.sch (star-delta starter).

tools.name: User Language examples (ex-*.ulp, useful-routines.ulp, ulpmessage.ulp, mkdir.ulp)
tools.description: Teaching examples for writing ULPs: ex-argv-path (argv and program path), ex-dialogs and ex-dlglist (dialog functions), ex-file-copy, ex-input-file (file dialog), ex-include with useful-routines.ulp (include files), ex-loop-lbrs (loop over all libraries and write error.txt) and ex-run-script (write and execute a script). ulpmessage.ulp shows a popup text and mkdir.ulp creates a subdirectory.
tools.usage: RUN ex-dialogs.ulp | RUN ulpmessage text | RUN mkdir subdirectoryname
tools.example:
RUN ulpmessage Board check finished
RUN mkdir cam-out
tools.notes: Good starting points together with the User Language chapter of the built-in help.
